title: Answer ceiling
what: The cut every verb's answer takes at 30,000 characters, keeping whole items and saying what was cut and how to ask for the rest.

title: Close line
what: One line per repository on a machine in which every close of that repository stands, keyed by its common git directory, holding the wide lane through each part of its check.

title: Declaration reader
what: Reads a repository's root testbed.toml into typed tables (test, projects, tools, check, build, deploy, runner, events), refusing unknown keys and another major, and finds the repository's root and paths.

title: Event hook
what: Sends a verb's event (deployed, deploy-failed, full-suite-failed, suite-flaky and the like) to the hook the environment or the declaration names, through sh with a JSON body; it never changes the verb's outcome.

title: Lanes and turn
what: The machine's wide and narrow lanes, each one queue lock in the temporary directory: taking a turn, the front and next ranks, held turns, kept places, the width a lane runs at, and the memory turn that retries a command killed for want of memory.

title: Languages
what: The language type in core and its members bun, node, cargo, browser and plain: what each claims as heavy, how it widens a command, reads a log, names and runs test files, and which configuration, root files and lockfile it answers for.

title: Placement
what: Where a run goes: here by default, or on another machine the declared placement endpoint names, its bench made ready over ssh and its output read back as an event stream.

title: Policy loader
what: The testbed's own fixed numbers and words, one TOML part per file under policy/, compiled into core and read once into deny_unknown_fields structs; fill_marks and fill_shown fill a line's {name} marks.

title: Run verb and status
what: The run verb, which runs one heavy command in its lane's turn or places it elsewhere, tells a run witness as it begins and ends, and ends on one result line or one command run; and the status verb's lines over each lane and the close line.
